title: Principles of Tooth Preparation I — Test

mcqs.q: The optimum restoration must satisfy which set of requirements together?
mcqs.explain: A successful restoration balances biologic, mechanical and esthetic requirements.

mcqs.q: The PREFERRED way to protect the adjacent tooth while breaking a proximal contact is to:
opts: Leave a thin lip of the proximal enamel of the tooth being prepared
Rely only on a metal matrix band
Ignore it, as reshaping restores the enamel fully
mcqs.explain: A thin protective lip of proximal enamel is preferred; a matrix band can perforate. Damaged enamel is more caries-prone even after polishing.

mcqs.q: Why is a damaged adjacent enamel surface more caries-prone even after polishing?
opts: Original surface enamel has higher fluoride and the disrupted layer retains more plaque
mcqs.explain: Surface enamel is more fluoride-rich; once interrupted it retains plaque and resists caries less.

mcqs.q: Which can cause irreversible pulpitis during tooth preparation?
opts: Extreme temperature, chemical irritation, or microorganisms
mcqs.explain: Heat, chemical irritants and bacteria can irreversibly injure the pulp; water spray and a light touch protect it.

mcqs.q: To minimize frictional heat when cutting with a high-speed handpiece, you should use:
opts: A feather-light, intermittent touch with a water spray
Heavy continuous pressure and no water
mcqs.explain: Light, intermittent cutting plus a water spray prevents the tooth from overheating.

mcqs.q: Before placing a foundation restoration for a fixed prosthesis, you must:
opts: Leave some caries under an indirect pulp cap
Seal the caries with a temporary only
Apply fluoride and restore over the caries
mcqs.explain: All carious dentine must be removed; an indirect pulp cap is not recommended under cast restorations because later failure jeopardizes the prosthesis.

mcqs.q: Tooth structure is conserved by, among other things:
opts: Using the minimum practical convergence angle (taper) between axial walls
Always choosing complete over partial coverage
Extending the margin as far apically as possible
mcqs.explain: Conservation: partial coverage, minimal taper, anatomic occlusal reduction, even axial reduction, conservative margins, and no unnecessary apical extension.

mcqs.q: Insufficient axial reduction most directly leads to:
opts: Overcontoured restorations that hamper plaque control
mcqs.explain: Under-reduced axial walls force overcontouring, which harbours plaque and promotes periodontal disease/caries, especially interproximally and at furcations.

mcqs.q: Typical occlusal clearance for the functional (buccal) cusp region is about:
mcqs.explain: Roughly: buccal ~1.5 mm, lingual ~1 mm, marginal ridges ~1 mm of clearance.

mcqs.q: A supra-erupted abutment tooth generally requires:
opts: More occlusal reduction than a normally positioned tooth
mcqs.explain: Supraeruption means more reduction is needed to create occlusal space; infra-occluded teeth need less.

mcqs.q: Whenever possible, the preparation margin should be:
mcqs.explain: Supragingival margins are easier to prepare, finish, keep clean, impress and evaluate, and sit on hard enamel.

mcqs.q: Which is a valid indication for a SUBGINGIVAL margin?
opts: Caries or an old restoration that extends subgingivally
A desire for the easiest possible impression
mcqs.explain: Subgingival is indicated for subgingival caries/erosion/restorations, proximal contact reaching the crest, extra retention/resistance, metal-ceramic esthetics, or uncontrolled root sensitivity.

mcqs.q: The junction between a cemented restoration and the tooth is important because it is a site for:
mcqs.explain: Luting-agent dissolution and roughness make the margin a nidus for plaque and recurrent caries; hence a smooth, well-adapted margin.

mcqs.q: Which finish line is classically formed as the negative image of a round-ended tapered diamond and favoured for metal margins?
mcqs.explain: A chamfer is produced by a round-ended diamond and gives a conservative, well-defined metal margin.

mcqs.q: A shoulder finish line is particularly indicated for:
opts: Esthetic all-ceramic crowns, to provide bulk for translucency
mcqs.explain: The shoulder provides the bulk of ceramic needed for strength and esthetics, at the cost of more tooth removal.

mcqs.q: Unsupported enamel at the margin must be removed because it:
opts: Fractures under load and leaves a marginal gap
mcqs.explain: Unsupported enamel breaks under function, opening a margin; all unsupported enamel should be removed and the wedging effect avoided.

mcqs.q: Tooth preparation is defined as:
opts: The mechanical alteration of a tooth to receive a restoration
The chemical conditioning of enamel before bonding
The removal of all carious dentine only
The shaping of a wax pattern to fit a die
mcqs.explain: We prepare teeth to create space for restorative material, establish a path of insertion and define a clean finish line.

mcqs.q: Which belongs to the MECHANICAL requirements of the optimum restoration?
opts: Retention form, resistance form and prevention of deformation
Conservation of tooth structure and supragingival margins
Minimum display of metal and maximum porcelain thickness
Harmonious occlusion and protection against fracture
mcqs.explain: The second and fourth are biologic requirements; the third is esthetic.

mcqs.q: Which belongs to the ESTHETIC requirements of the optimum restoration?
opts: Minimum display of metal and maximum porcelain thickness
mcqs.explain: Porcelain occlusal surfaces and subgingival margins where needed are the other esthetic requirements.

mcqs.q: Damage to the tongue and cheeks during preparation is prevented by:
opts: Careful retraction with an aspirator tip, mouth mirror or flanged saliva ejector
A metal matrix band around the adjacent tooth
mcqs.explain: Great care is needed to protect the tongue when preparing the lingual surfaces of mandibular molars.

mcqs.q: The pulp chamber and horns recede with age because of:
opts: Sclerosis of the dentinal tubules only
mcqs.explain: A younger tooth has larger, more coronally-placed pulp horns that are easier to expose during reduction.

mcqs.q: To minimise thermal injury with a high-speed handpiece, the operator should use:
opts: A feather-light touch with a water spray and intermittent cutting
Firm pressure with air coolant only
mcqs.explain: Even with a light touch, the tooth overheats unless a water spray is used.

mcqs.q: Which dental materials are named as causes of CHEMICAL pulpal injury?
opts: Bases, restorative resins, solvents and luting agents
mcqs.explain: Bacterial injury, by contrast, comes from bacteria left behind or entering via microleakage.

mcqs.q: An indirect pulp cap is NOT recommended on a tooth that will receive a cast restoration because:
opts: Later failure would jeopardise extensive treatment
It would not set under a cemented crown
It causes galvanic currents with the alloy
It prevents the impression material from setting
mcqs.explain: All carious dentine must be removed before placing a foundation restoration for a fixed prosthesis.

mcqs.q: The ideal total occlusal convergence (taper) between axial walls is about:
mcqs.explain: An excessive taper such as 20° results in considerable loss of tooth structure and weaker retention.

mcqs.q: Compared with an anatomically contoured occlusal preparation, a FLAT occlusal preparation gives:
opts: Either insufficient clearance or excessive reduction
A more conservative result in every case
mcqs.explain: Reducing on the anatomic planes gives adequate clearance without excessive reduction.

mcqs.q: The minimum occlusal clearance stated for the BUCCAL cusp is:
mcqs.explain: The lingual cusp and the marginal ridges and fossae each require 1.0 mm.

mcqs.q: A mandibular molar is typically inclined how far lingually, which the path of placement must respect?
mcqs.explain: The path of placement should coincide with the long axis of the tooth; a severely malaligned tooth may be orthodontically repositioned first.

mcqs.q: Which is one of the five criteria of good MARGIN GEOMETRY?
opts: Ease of identification in the impression and on the die
Extension into the furcation for retention
mcqs.explain: The others are ease of preparation without overextension or unsupported enamel, a distinct boundary for finishing the wax pattern, sufficient bulk of material, and conservation of tooth structure.

mcqs.q: Which finish line is the MOST conservative, but gives a thin margin that is hard to read on the die?
mcqs.explain: It also risks over- or under-contouring of the restoration.

mcqs.q: The 'wedging effect' that can split a remaining tooth is minimised by:
opts: Rounding the internal line angles of the preparation
mcqs.explain: Sharp internal line angles, or restoration designs that act like a wedge, concentrate stress. No tooth is unbreakable.

mcqs.q: An abutment tooth that has SUPRAERUPTED generally requires:
opts: Less occlusal reduction than a tooth in normal occlusion
mcqs.explain: An infraoccluded abutment, by contrast, needs less occlusal reduction than a tooth in normal occlusion.

saqs.q: List the three biologic considerations of tooth preparation.
saqs.a: Prevention of damage during preparation (adjacent teeth, soft tissues, pulp) · conservation of tooth structure · considerations affecting future dental health (axial reduction, margin placement, geometry, occlusion, preventing fracture).

list: Prevention of damage during preparation — adjacent teeth, soft tissues, pulp
Considerations affecting future dental health — axial reduction, margin placement/adaptation/geometry, occlusion, preventing fracture

saqs.q: How is the pulp protected during tooth preparation? Give the three causes of pulpal injury.
saqs.a: Protect with a feather-light intermittent touch and copious water spray, respecting pulp-chamber morphology (smaller with age). Causes: TEMPERATURE (frictional heat) · CHEMICAL (bases, resins, solvents, luting agents) · BACTERIAL (microleakage) — so remove all carious dentine.

ans.text: Protect with a feather-light, intermittent touch and copious water spray; respect pulp-chamber morphology (smaller with age).

saqs.q: List four guidelines for conserving tooth structure.
saqs.a: Partial rather than complete coverage · minimum practical convergence angle · reduce the occlusal surface along anatomic planes · remove axial structure evenly · select a conservative margin · avoid unnecessary apical extension.

list: Reduce the occlusal surface along the anatomic planes, for uniform thickness
Remove axial structure evenly — reposition orthodontically if needed

saqs.q: State the advantages of a supragingival margin and two indications for a subgingival margin.
saqs.a: SUPRAGINGIVAL — easy to prepare and finish without tissue trauma · on hard enamel · easily kept plaque-free · easier impressions · easily evaluated. SUBGINGIVAL indications — subgingival caries/erosion/old restoration · contact reaching the gingival crest · extra retention needed · metal-ceramic esthetics · uncontrolled root sensitivity.

head: SUPRAGINGIVAL advantages
SUBGINGIVAL indications
rows: easy to prepare and finish accurately, without soft-tissue trauma
subgingival caries, erosion or old restoration
proximal contact reaching the gingival crest
easily evaluated at placement and recall

saqs.q: Name the common finish-line (margin) types and state which is preferred for a metal margin and which for an esthetic all-ceramic crown.
saqs.a: Types: feather edge, knife edge, chamfer, bevel, shoulder, bevelled shoulder. CHAMFER is preferred for a metal margin (conservative, well-defined). SHOULDER is preferred for an esthetic all-ceramic crown (bulk for translucency and strength).

head: For a METAL margin
For an ALL-CERAMIC crown
rows: the SHOULDER — bulk for translucency and strength

saqs.q: List the three sets of requirements the optimum restoration must satisfy, with examples of each.
saqs.a: BIOLOGIC — conservation, no overcontouring, supragingival margins, harmonious occlusion, protection against fracture. MECHANICAL — retention form, resistance form, prevention of deformation. ESTHETIC — minimum metal display, maximum porcelain thickness, porcelain occlusal surfaces, subgingival margins where needed. The optimum restoration satisfies all three together.

head: Set
Examples
rows: conservation of tooth structure · avoidance of overcontouring · supragingival margins · harmonious occlusion · protection against fracture
retention form · resistance form · prevention of deformation
minimum display of metal · maximum porcelain thickness · porcelain occlusal surfaces · subgingival margins where needed

ans.text: The optimum restoration satisfies all three together.

saqs.q: Describe the three causes of injury to the pulp during tooth preparation and how each is avoided.
saqs.a: TEMPERATURE — friction generates heat; a feather-light touch with a high-speed handpiece minimises it, but a water spray is still needed, with intermittent cutting. CHEMICAL — bases, restorative resins, solvents and luting agents. BACTERIAL — bacteria left behind or entering by microleakage; remove all carious dentine, and an indirect pulp cap is NOT recommended under cast restorations, since later failure jeopardises extensive treatment.

head: Cause
Detail and avoidance
rows: considerable heat from friction between rotary instrument and tooth. A feather-light touch with a high-speed handpiece removes material with minimal heat — but the tooth still overheats unless a water spray is used; use intermittent cutting
the chemical action of bases, restorative resins, solvents and luting agents

bacteria left behind or entering via microleakage. Remove all carious dentine before a foundation restoration; an indirect pulp cap is NOT recommended on teeth receiving cast restorations, since later failure jeopardises extensive treatment
